summary: Approved development note that sets the handoff fields a pilot lot must carry from development to the scale team. It covers recipe card identity, concentrations in mg/mL, loading in weight percent, dose and particle size assumptions in µm, and the manufacturability risks still open before the scale gate.

title_block.title: Pilot Lot Handoff: Required Fields for Recipe Cards
title_block.subtitle: Development note, approved before the scale gate

blocks.p: This note defines the fields that must travel with a pilot lot from development to the scale team. The aim is that the scale gate review works from the same information the bench used, rather than from a verbal account of it.

The note applies to pilot lots made from a locked recipe card. Exploratory screens are not handed off this way. Their results stay on the bench sheets and are cited from there, so a screen is never mistaken for a locked process.
Every field below is required. A handoff with a blank field is returned to the sender before the scale team opens the lot record.

rows: Card number, revision letter and issue date
mg/mL for each stock and for the final formulation
Weight percent for each component, with the basis stated
Dose level, its basis per kg or per unit, and the source of the assumption
D50 and span in µm, the method and the date measured
Storage location as recorded by Sample Management
Each open manufacturability risk, its owner and the date it must close
table.caption: Table 1 Handoff fields

blocks.p: Loading is always given in weight percent with the basis stated, for example weight of active per total weight of the final blend. Concentrations in mg/mL are given separately and are never used in place of a loading.

A dose assumption is a design basis, not a tested outcome. The handoff must say so. An assumption written as though it were a result will be returned, because the scale team will otherwise build the lot plan on it.

Higher loading improves the dose delivered per unit of blend but raises the viscosity risk at pilot scale. Where a lead formulation is selected on dose grounds, the trade-off against that risk is written into the handoff in one short paragraph, not left for the scale team to find.

Particle sizes are given in µm. The handoff states the measurement method and whether the sample was wet or dry. Where the material is measured both before and after blending, both values are given, with the blend step named, so a change in size can be traced to the step that caused it.
Milling conditions are recorded on the recipe card and not repeated in the note. The note records only the outcome that the scale team needs to match.
The following risks were open when this note was approved. Each has a named owner and must be closed or accepted before the scale gate.

list: Blend flow at the selected loading has not yet been checked on a pilot blender. This is to be done before the scale gate.
One excipient is sensitive to moisture. The storage conditions for the lot are to be confirmed with Sample Management.
Particle size drifts on milling between runs. Size is to be re-measured on each pilot lot and not carried forward from the last one.
The dose assumption depends on a single literature basis that the group has not yet checked against its own bench data.

blocks.p: Risks that are accepted rather than closed are signed off by the formulation development lead, with the reason written next to the risk.

This note is approved for use from the date of issue. It replaces the informal handoff email used for the previous pilot lots. The local master applies to this note during the transition period, and the recipe card and accession numbers quoted in it are the local ones.
